notes: ACCESS: leroymerlin.fr is fully live (not retired/redirected -- confirmed via robots.txt sitemap reference and current Google-indexed product/category URLs) but the entire origin returns HTTP 403 (server header 'LMCDN', Fastly-fronted, body 'Varnish cache server') to every request from this workstation, with NO variation across route or fingerprint -- exhausted Rule 2: (1) direct fetch 403; (2) curl_cffi impersonation swept 20+ profiles (chrome99-136, safari15_5-18_0 incl. iOS, edge, firefox) -- identical 403/420-byte body on every one, indicating an IP/ASN or geo-level block at the Fastly edge rather than a TLS-fingerprint bot challenge; (3) r.jina.ai retried 4x over ~40s -- consistent 'may require CAPTCHA' empty response (PerimeterX behind the edge); (4) translate.goog -- HTTP 400 serving a PerimeterX ('ppConfig') challenge page, origin refuses Google's fetcher; (5) WebFetch -- 403; (6) side doors (robots.txt, sitemap-index.xml, legacy /v3/search/search.do, /api/ guesses) -- all 403 identically; (7) no AAAA record for www.leroymerlin.fr or its Fastly SNI pool, so no IPv6 route available. robots.txt (recovered via Wayback) has NO ClaudeBot/anthropic-ai-specific disallow -- standard 'User-agent: *' rules only, so this is a network/WAF block, not a bot policy opt-out. STRUCTURE: full category tree recovered from Wayback Machine snapshots (Dec 2025 for the lighting '/produits/luminaire/' tree, which is also confirmed live via current Google search indexing of leroymerlin.fr product/category URLs; Jan 2025 for the '/produits/decoration-eclairage/' decor tree) per Rule 2's Wayback-for-structure allowance. Per Rule 1, Wayback counts are NEVER used as qty -- every row here carries qty:null with a MANUAL REVIEW flag; this is a deliberate correct-null outcome per the project's null-is-a-correct-answer rule, not a coverage gap. SCOPE (Rule 0 + DIY-chain caution): as expected for a Kingfisher/ADEO DIY chain, the vast majority of the catalogue (hardware, building materials, plumbing, tools, paint, flooring, furniture) is out of scope and was not extracted. Genuine decor sub-tree extracted: Lighting (every fixture type, full Lighting-by-Room branch incl. bathroom/kitchen/bedroom/dressing/garage per Rule 0.1, full Outdoor Lighting branch per Rule 0.5 incl. garden/pool/terrace, and a Professional Lighting branch -- included under Rule 0 product-type-beats-room/venue-name since these are still lighting fixtures, just marketed to a B2B/commercial buyer segment; documented here as an overlap-risk branch since some products may duplicate the residential fixture types above), Wall Decor & Mirrors (mirrors, photo frames, wall clocks, canvas art, posters, decorative plaques, decorative wall objects), and Home Accessories (vases, candle holders, statuettes, tabletop decor objects, and curtain rods/rails/cables -- explicitly in-scope per brief's 'decorative metal' bullet). EXCLUDED and why: ceiling fans and bulbs/LED tubes (ampoule-et-led, tube-led -- explicit exclusion); 'luminaire-diy' (DIY lighting-component builder, functional parts) and 'creez-votre-luminaire'; 'luminaire-par-matiere' (lighting-by-material) and per-type style sub-facets (lampe-design, lampe-pop, lampadaire-industriel, applique-murale-design, plafonnier-design, lustre-industriel) as facet/style re-cuts of the type leaves already counted above; 'eclairage-public' (public/street lighting -- municipal infrastructure, not a home-decor product); 'nouveautes-luminaire', 'nos-series-de-luminaires-exterieurs', 'luminaires-de-designers', 'luminaires-coordonnes' and 'boutique-du-designer' (New Arrivals / curated collections / designer-brand landing pages -- navigation, not categories); the entire 'adhesif-decoratif' node (8 of 9 children are functional adhesive film/backsplash/window/appliance/furniture stickers; the one plausibly-decor child 'stickers-muraux' was dropped with the mixed roll-up rather than padding); 'dalle-rosace-et-moulure' (architectural ceiling mouldings/rosettes -- construction trim, not decorative accessory); 'tableau-pense-bete' (memo/whiteboard -- functional office item); 'barre-de-vitrage' and 'barre-pour-porte-lucarne-et-ciel-de-lit' under the curtain-rod node (glazing bars / dormer-door bars -- functional window/structural hardware, not curtain rods); all textiles (rideau-voilage-et-vitrage, tapis, coussin-plaid-et-pouf, linge-de-lit, linge-de-bain, linge-de-lit-enfant, literie-enfant, store/blinds); 'plante-artificielle' (faux plants -- explicit exclusion); 'decoration-chambre-enfant' siblings 'toute-decoration-enfant' (All), 'sol-et-mur-chambre-enfant' (flooring/wallcovering) and 'decoration-plus-responsable-pour-chambre-enfants' (curated eco collection); 'les-petits-prix-deco-a-moins-de-50-euro' (price-filter landing page). RULE 0 GAIN: without Rule 0 this extraction would likely have stopped at the flat fixture-type list and skipped the entire Lighting-by-Room branch (Living Room, Bathroom, Kitchen, Adult/Kids Bedroom, Dressing, Garage/Cellar/Attic) and the entire Outdoor Lighting branch (11 nodes incl. garden, pool, terrace) purely because of their room/venue words -- both were kept in full, plus bathroom lighting specifically and the professional/commercial fixture branch, per Rule 0's product-type-over-room-name principle.
